headline: OpenAI Debuts New ChatGPT Payment Method With Card Networks
author: Natalie Lung

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a new secure payment method that its artificial intelligence tool can use to make purchases on consumers' behalf, renewing its push into AI shopping after winding down an Instant Checkout feature earlier this year.

The virtual wallet, built in partnership with American Express Co., Mastercard Inc. and Visa Inc., lets users add a card once and approve each purchase without reentering their payment details, OpenAI said in a statement Friday. AI agents handling the purchase don't have access to users' actual card details, and each transaction will require biometric verification, such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan.

The new system will initially be available through OpenAI's Dots agent tool for US subscribers of its Pro tier, according to the statement. It's not available in Chat or Work interfaces, or in standalone threads on OpenAI's Codex programming platform. The tool will initially be available to a limited number of users so it "can learn from real-world use and work with businesses, banks and payment networks to improve compatibility and reliability," the company said.

The wallet marks a fresh attempt by OpenAI to help its 1.2 billion ChatGPT weekly users make purchases, as newer competitors like Meta Platforms Inc.'s Muse and xAI's Grok Bot also tout similar capabilities.

ChatGPT introduced Instant Checkout in September 2025 to manage purchases of items within the ChatGPT chat interface, but it required brands to provide OpenAI with updated product inventory. In March, ChatGPT shelved the feature and said payments were moving into individual plug-in apps that third-party brands built for the assistant to "better meet merchants and users where they are," so that "purchases can happen more seamlessly," a spokesperson said at the time. The startup said it would focus on "making ChatGPT search and product discovery great."

With the new wallet, ChatGPT's agent, which is able to do things on the web for users, can more flexibly make purchases on any e-commerce website, even if a brand doesn't have a ChatGPT plug-in. But that assumes the site isn't blocking the agent tools.

The capabilities could mark a new flashpoint between AI assistants and brand websites, which have increasingly barred bots to preserve data control and relationships with customers — and, by extension, ad revenue. On Wednesday, United Airlines Holdings Inc. became the latest seller to block agents, joining the likes of Amazon.com Inc. and eBay Inc.
"To accept payment from ChatGPT Wallet, websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents," OpenAI said.
